subject: Unexpected mid-cycle reclassification causing token delta - request for evidence
messages:
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brightcart.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected mid-cycle token reclass and invoice delta

Kimberly —

We received the November invoice and there is a ~28% token increase attributed to a reclassification between ratebands on 2026-11-02. BrightCart did not change traffic patterns, and our app logs show identical request volumes. Can you share the evidence for the reclassification and how the tokens were bucketed?

We need:
- Metering export for our org (Granular per-request counts and rateband labels) for 2026-10-28 to 2026-11-15
- Any system release notes or model/quantization changes around 2026-11-01 -> 2026-11-03
- A point-in-time sample showing the tokenization differences for identical inputs

We are pausing payment on the disputed portion until we get that evidence — please escalate.

Thanks,
Evan

BrightCart

Subject: Fwd: Unexpected mid-cycle token reclass and invoice delta

Kimberly / Marcus —

I pulled an initial export and a short summary: the platform automated rateband tagger applied a different token classification for a small subset of streaming sessions between 2026-11-01T23:50:00Z and 2026-11-02T02:10:00Z. That window lines up with a hotfix deploy to the session-slicing service (non-ML) but we need to verify whether downstream tokenization paths were affected.

Attached: usage_snapshot_20261101-20261115.csv (per-request rows), session_sample_20261102.txt (raw request/response for three sample requestIDs).

Initial notes:
- Total affected requests: ~14,200 (0.9% of BrightCart’s windowed requests)
- Token delta skew: those requests show a 3.4x token increase due to a shift from prefix-compression being applied to full-delta encoding in the metering pipeline for streaming responses.
- No model-version rollouts were scheduled that night in Hub (checked: hubspot id DC-7831 activity shows no model pin change).

Next: Marcus, can you validate kernel logs + commit hashes for the tokenization path and confirm if the hotfix touched the metering pipeline? I’ll follow up with a limited provisional credit proposal once we have scope confirmed.

-ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Liu <evan.liu@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle token reclass and invoice delta

Ben / Kimberly / Evan —

I dug into the runtime traces and metering worker logs. Summary: the hotfix to session-slicing inadvertently toggled a flag that bypassed prefix-compression metadata for streaming responses that contained nested function-call outputs. When the metering exporter reconstructs token segments, it misclassified those segments into a higher rateband.

Evidence attached and annotated: session_sample_20261102.txt (lines prefixed with >> show token boundaries reconstructed by the exporter). The flow:
- session-slicing hotfix (commit a4b7f9) changed a predicate used by downstream composer to mark compressed prefixes as "skip-for-export"
- Exporter then treated the entire response as expanded text which increased token counts reported to billing

Impact estimate:~14.2k requests for BrightCart, producing +1.05M billable tokens in the window (approx +27% on that invoice line).

Mitigation:
1) We reverted the predicate at 2026-11-02T03:00:00Z — no additional requests after that are affected.
2) We will re-run the exporter with corrected prefix-compression markers and provide a corrected CSV.
3) Recommend a provisional credit for the disputed amount while we finish the re-export and verification.

Evan — I’ll run the corrected export now and post a signed checksums file to the shared drive. ETA for re-export and checksum: 12 hours.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle token reclass and invoice delta — provisional credit and next steps

Evan —

Thank you for your patience. Attached is the corrected exporter output (we placed it in the shared drive link below) along with checksums and an annotated sample. Key points: 
- Root cause: an unintended predicate change in a session-slicing hotfix (commit a4b7f9) caused prefix-compressed segments to be exported as full text for a 2h20m window on 2026-11-02.
- Scope for BrightCart: ~14,200 requests / +1.05M billable tokens (we’ve validated 3 independent samples).
- Action taken: reverted change on 2026-11-02T03:00:00Z; re-exported and validated.

Resolution proposal:
1) Provisionally credit BrightCart for the disputed tokens on the November invoice while we complete a full re-export audit (expected within 48 hours).
2) We will issue a corrected invoice for the November period and remove the disputed line-item.
3) Engineering will add a canary gate for exporter predicates to prevent recurrence.

Please confirm you accept the provisional credit path and whether you want a short (30-min) call to review the technical evidence.

Shared evidence: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/brightcart-metering-evidence
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/BR-2219

Best,
Kimberly Park
